gaps.sentence: The man ___ wallet I found works at the post office.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose wallet' means 'the man's wallet'; 'who's' means 'who is' and cannot precede a noun.

gaps.sentence: The discussion got to a stage ___ nobody was listening any more.
gaps.explanation: 'A stage where ...' means 'a stage at which ...'; the clause has its own subject and verb, so 'which' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: The author ___ books sell millions worldwide lives in Iceland.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the author to her books; 'who' could not be followed directly by 'books'.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.hint: after 'all', the relative pronoun is not 'what'
gaps.explanation: 'All that glitters' is the proverb pattern; 'what' cannot follow 'all', and 'which' is avoided after 'all'.

gaps.sentence: ___ surprised me most was his calm.
gaps.hint: 'what' = the thing that; the sentence has no other subject
gaps.explanation: 'What' means 'the thing that' and acts as subject: 'What surprised me most ...' — 'that' cannot introduce this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: We arrived at the hotel at noon, ___ the rooms were not ready.
gaps.explanation: 'When' introduces non-defining clauses about time after a comma; 'that' is impossible after a comma.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.
